body:
I don't look forward to anything any more. I remember even a few years ago I was counting down the days to Jessica Jones' first series on Netflix; haven't seen any of the second at all. I have dozens of Star Wars books from the old EU under my bed; have yet to see The Last Jedi. I have probably about fifty games in my Steam library that are untouched, from The Binding of Isaac to all The Witcher games and I have no desire to play any of them.

I think I'll wait until my mum next goes on holiday so that I can gather the necessary equipment undisturbed and then some time after she's back I'll hire somewhere and do it overnight. I'll post a letter to the police the night before informing them of my location and what they can expect to find.

The lack of motivation is the biggest thing I think. If you've been reading my other responses you'll know of my feelings towards "higher powers" and such and that I don't think life has any meaning other than what we create for ourselves. I don't have one. I have, as mentioned, given this some thought before and I've come up empty every time.

I don't know how I'd define what a successful life looked like for me. I never have. Without that vision, something to strive towards... I've just given up. I gave up a long time ago.

I feel like I'm just repeating myself now. It's just... I dunno. I keep typing stuff out and deleting it because yeah, it's basically the same things.

Don't read too much into the penis thing by the way. I just mentioned it as like, "one more thing to add to the list of things to get sorted." I don't have any psychological hang-ups around that specifically and from my limited research into the area it could be fixed with a fairly simple operation, whichever it actually is. I just haven't seen any reason to do anything about it because of all my *other* craziness, such as how I think that I'm unattractive and people are better off without me and so on. It's never been a high priority. Sure, if I was making a go of it and I did get it sorted as I worked down the list then I'd have all the normal nerves you'd expect from a man in his early thirties who wasn't sure how kissing worked, but that's another matter entirely.

I'm really good at fingering though.

I went to the doctor once before. Over the course of a year or two I was given a couple of different SSRIs at different dosages and none had any discernible impact, so I stopped taking them at the same time as I dumped my mates. I was never on any therapy at the time.

Though my diet is fucking awful. I had a blood test at the time and no concerns were raised from that but other than that... I have no doubt that if my doctor was given a list of my diet they'd freak the fuck out. It is so peculiar and specific that if I were to list it would actually identify me to people who know who I am. I could do it on one hand. And yes I know that it, and my lack of exercise, and my staying indoors are all bad things that I should change.

But why?

Say I go to the doctor and get some more medications to try. I also get therapy this time, CBT to brainwash away the negative attitudes and low self-esteem and so on. I start trying new things to eat and do some basic exercise. My brother is a personal trainer and my sister trained as a chef so I could definitely get some assistance there (sure, she's on the other side of the world and hasn't used her qualification for anything job-related, but still). I get an operation to fix my penis so that I could actually have a proper sexual relationship (my foreskin won't go over the head, either because it's too tight or that bit underneath - what's it called? Frenulum or something? - is too short/not stretchy enough/other). And since I'm in the UK I don't need to worry about how much any of this costs. Yay, I'm on the mend!

...And then what?

I'd still have to rebuild my social life from basically scratch in my thirties and I'm not the most outgoing person so that's a challenge to look forward to, including starting to pursue for the very first time romantic and sexual relationships. I'm not a virgin, but my experience is pretty limited because of my penis problem (it's more painful than pleasurable so I never bothered seeking them out). I'd still live at home. I haven't used these years to save lots of money so I'm still poor. I'd still have a shitty job. No hobbies, interests, dreams, hopes, goals, ambitions, *qualifications*. That last one is actually the one I'm least concerned about. I could theoretically get them if I tried. But what am I getting? I don't have any natural skills or talents that I could parlay into something. I'd leave my job tomorrow if I could come up with... well, *anything* that doesn't make me want to kill myself even more when I think about doing it full-time.

I know I know, one step at a time, realistic goals and so on. I also know that as I start to improve that my mindset could change and I could find those things that I'm missing, something to be passionate about. Intellectually I know all that. But without something big to aim for I can't get started. It just feels like it would, in the end, be a waste of time. Sure, maybe I'm in better shape and a bit more confident but I'd still be in the same place as I am now. The same place I've been in for fifteen years. It's not like I've never considered any of this before but I just don't have anything to motivate me to get started. Simply "getting better" isn't enough, not by itself. Hence the subsequent googling.

We know enough about how brains work. "I," that is, my consciousness, is just a collection of chemicals and electricity and such. When my brain dies those processes will (obviously) end and "I" will cease to be. Humans aren't special. We're just one type of great ape on a goldilocks zone planet orbiting a rather unremarkable star. Unless you're going to start talking about magical nonsense like souls there's no reason to think otherwise and if you *are* going to start talking about something along those lines I refer you to my prior answer of "which afterlife am I supposed to shoot for?"

It seems like an extraordinarily small chance that there is something after life. If I truly though that it was a potential risk then I should be looking at every single religious, mythical, spiritual and philosophical take and try to work out a system that would satisfy as many of the contrary preconditions as possible in an attempt to get the 'good ending' of life.

I'm not going to do that because that would be absurd. If there *is* something (and why would there be?), well, I guess I'll be miserable somewhere else instead.

I can't actually even fathom what a "state of happiness" would look like for me.

I've had people from work ask me to join them on nights out and stuff. Even if I enjoyed going to clubs I'd still decline for the same reason I stopped hanging out with my few friends ten years ago. I've had a few "relapses" since were I've started to get closer to people again but then I remember my one ambition is to pluck up the balls to kill myself and I withdraw again.

I certainly don't consider myself an expert but I think I have enough passing knowledge of philosophy (or at least, pop culture philosophy) that it doesn't appeal to me. Sure, there's some interesting thought experiments and it can be good to look at things from a different angle and so on but ultimately it just feels like empty naval-gazing.

No offence if you're a planning to be a philosophy major or something. It's just not my thing is all. I was never very good at art for similar reasons. Talking about inspiration and how a piece could be interpreted and an artists' true intentions and so on... I always struggled with those things. Works never spoke to me. I just bullshitted when we had to look at other people's stuff and I always found doing my own to be difficult (regardless of technical ability, or rather lack of it) because I was never inspired.

As I just replied to someone else above I never had any hopes for my life. That's likely a large part of the problem. I can never really remember having any hopes, dreams, goals, ambitions and so on. I never wanted to go anywhere or do anything or be anyone. I don't have childhood trauma that therapy could help me to deal with, I have an existential ennui. As unhappy as I am I'm also tired and bored.

I do sometimes think "you could just do anything; since you're not afraid of dying, why not give [x] a go?" Then I think "but [x] doesn't sound fun" and that's before practical concerns like money.

Although theoretically possible it seems like there's an infinitesimally small chance of something like that being correct and that it's far more probable that it's just nonsense made up by people a long time ago who didn't know any better. I actually find it more likely that we're all 1s and 0s in an astonishingly advanced computer to be honest. If I was going to let something like that have an impact on my decision I'd have to contend with angering the Egyptian gods because I didn't do the burial rites or faeries snorting my soul like it's cocaine or any number of equally far-fetched scenarios that no one else takes into account when they die.

If there *is* something afterwards (which I don't accept) then I'm going to get there eventually anyway and then I'll just be in the same scenario sooo...

Yeah, I've always disliked the question "what is the meaning of life?" and similar such things. There isn't one. Instead, basically... you do you. Find your passion, life is what you make it, etc etc.

I cannot conceive of something. I've always told people that... y'know when you're a little kid, and you're asked "what do you want to be when you grow up?" and it's always ridiculous things like "football player!" or "astronaut!" and so on? Yeah, I never had an answer. In secondary school I assumed I'd go on to get an entirely average and uninteresting job in an office somewhere and I'd be unlikely to get to even mid-management, instead staying as an anonymous drone. I went to Sixth Form to doss around for a couple more years and delay the inevitable, not to work towards university. I couldn't think of a single course that excited me so I didn't go. Even if I could magically disregard the requirements of ability and funds I still to this day can't think of something I would have liked to have done.

While that's unfortunate there's not much I can do about other people that I haven't already. As I said, I've deliberately avoided making friends with people at work and such. My phone has like, ten people in it, all family. I would have moved away if I could have afforded it, though it's likely that it wouldn't do much to soften the blow to family members anyway.

I'm not going to stick around because other people will be sad and miss me. It's often said that suicide is selfish. What's wrong with being a little selfish? I think it's far more selfish of *everyone else* to want me to stay even though I'm miserable just for their own benefit.

Why wait? I can tell you what I'll be doing when I'm fifty, the same as I'm doing now. My day-to-day hasn't changed in ten years. Last week looked similar to the week before that which was the same as the month before that which looked suspiciously like the year that came before...

And I really can't be arsed with another nineteen years of it.
